heading: EXT. FUNERAL HOME PARKING LOT - FOOD TRUCK - DAY

units.text: EXT. FUNERAL HOME PARKING LOT - FOOD TRUCK - DAY
A tamale truck parked between hearses.
Mourners in black stand in line holding paper plates.
Six Castellanos-Whitfields.
One truck.
ABUELA FLORENTINA, eighties, in a black lace mantilla, orders for everyone.
Her son, ARTURO, fifties, pays.
Her daughter-in-law, KATHLEEN, fifties, wipes her eyes with a napkin.
Their daughters, IMANI, twenties, and DAHLIA, teens, argue over hot sauce.
Their cousin, BASIL, thirties, eats from two plates.
Arturo, she wants pork. Give the girl pork.
units.name: FLORENTINA

units.text: Mama, she's vegetarian.
units.name: ARTURO

units.text: I'm not vegetarian!
units.name: IMANI

units.text: Imani, you've been a vegetarian since June.
units.name: DAHLIA

units.text: Dahlia, mind your own plate!
units.name: IMANI

units.text: Girls. Please. It's your grandfather's day.
units.name: KATHLEEN

units.text: He'd have loved this.
units.name: BASIL

units.text: He hated tamales.
units.name: FLORENTINA

units.text: He'd have loved the fight.
units.name: BASIL

units.text: A silence.
Then, one by one, they start to laugh.
